import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Read the source file
filepath = '/app/Household_Appliances.xlsx'

# Read all rows with no header to get raw data
df_raw = pd.read_excel(filepath, header=None)

# Row 0 is top header, row 1 is sub-header, data starts from row 2
df = df_raw.iloc[2:].copy()
df.columns = df_raw.iloc[1].values  # Use row 1 as column names

# Set Time as index for easier handling
df['Time'] = pd.to_datetime(df.iloc[:, 0])

# Column groups for each appliance:
# Refrigerators: cols 1,2,3,4
# Air Conditioners: cols 5,6,7,8
# Washing Machines: cols 9,10,11,12
appliance_names = ['Household Refrigerators', 'Air Conditioners', 'Household Washing Machines']
metric_names = ['Current Period Sales(Ten Thousand Units)',
                'Accumulated Sales (Ten Thousand Units)',
                'Year-on-Year Growth (%)',
                'Accumulated Growth (%)']
col_groups = [
    (df.columns[1], df.columns[2], df.columns[3], df.columns[4]),   # Refrigerators
    (df.columns[5], df.columns[6], df.columns[7], df.columns[8]),   # Air Conditioners
    (df.columns[9], df.columns[10], df.columns[11], df.columns[12]) # Washing Machines
]

result_rows = []

for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    time_val = row.iloc[0]  # Original Time value
    if pd.isna(time_val):
        continue
    
    # Check if this month has at least some data across all appliances
    has_data = False
    for group_idx, group_cols in enumerate(col_groups):
        for col in group_cols:
            if not pd.isna(row[col]):
                has_data = True
                break
        if has_data:
            break
    
    if not has_data:
        continue
    
    # Get month string in YYYY-MM format
    if pd.isna(time_val):
        time_str = ''
    else:
        try:
            t = pd.Timestamp(time_val)
            time_str = t.strftime('%Y-%m')
        except:
            time_str = str(time_val)[:7]
    
    for group_idx, (c0, c1, c2, c3) in enumerate(col_groups):
        current_sales = row[c0]
        accum_sales = row[c1]
        yoy_growth = row[c2]
        accum_growth = row[c3]
        
        # Multiply growth values by 100 to convert to percentage
        if not pd.isna(yoy_growth):
            yoy_growth = yoy_growth * 100
        if not pd.isna(accum_growth):
            accum_growth = accum_growth * 100
        
        # Determine if there's any data in this appliance's row
        # Check current_sales and accum_sales - at least one should be non-NaN
        if pd.isna(current_sales) and pd.isna(accum_sales):
            continue
        
        result_rows.append({
            'Time': time_str,
            'Appliance types': appliance_names[group_idx],
            'Current Period Sales(Ten Thousand Units)': current_sales,
            'Accumulated Sales (Ten Thousand Units)': accum_sales,
            'Year-on-Year Growth (%)': yoy_growth,
            'Accumulated Growth (%)': accum_growth
        })

result_df = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)

# Sort by Time in reverse chronological order
result_df['SortKey'] = pd.to_datetime(result_df['Time'], format='%Y-%m')
result_df = result_df.sort_values('SortKey', ascending=False).drop(columns=['SortKey']).reset_index(drop=True)

print(f'Output rows: {len(result_df)}')
print(f'Output columns: {list(result_df.columns)}')
print(result_df.head(10).to_string())
print('...')
print(result_df.tail(10).to_string())

# Save to Excel
result_df.to_excel('/app/Processed.xlsx', index=False, engine='xlsxwriter')
print('\nSaved to /app/Processed.xlsx')
